title: At a Ballroom Evening
description: Step into a dance hall through familiar dance names, partner roles, and smooth movement words.
cardDescription: Step into a dance hall through familiar dance names, partner roles, and smooth movement words.
focus: The clues define dance vocabulary without requiring a routine. A named dance differs from an action within it.
solvingTip: Look for a dance name, a partner role, or a movement across the floor.
words: Ballroom dance traditionally counted in three beats
Partner dance strongly associated with Argentina
Latin partner dance with Cuban roots
Smooth ballroom dance in common four-beat time
Lively dance associated with a quick duple rhythm
Role guiding the direction of a partner dance
To respond to a partner’s guiding dance movement
One placement of the foot in dancing
Change of facing direction while dancing
To move smoothly across a dance floor
Surface on which ballroom partners dance
To move in a patterned way to music

answerNotes.WALTZ: The waltz is traditionally in triple time. The three-beat count helps distinguish it from many four-beat dances.
answerNotes.FOXTROT: Foxtrot names a smooth ballroom form. The clue does not ask for the animal suggested by its spelling.
answerNotes.LEAD: Lead is a guiding role in a partner dance. It is pronounced like leed in this sense.
answerNotes.POLKA: Polka is a lively dance with a duple feel. It is distinct from the three-beat waltz.

title: On the Square-Dance Floor
description: Join a square-dance scene through familiar formations, partner actions, and the voice guiding the figures.
cardDescription: Join a square-dance scene through familiar formations, partner actions, and the voice guiding the figures.
focus: The clues describe positions and actions through plain meanings. A few traditional figure names are explained directly.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names a person, an arrangement, or a dance figure.
words: Two people dancing as a pair
Formation of four couples facing around a central space
Round formation made by joined dancers
Figure in which partners walk together around the set
Figure in which dancers pass around each other without turning
Turning figure performed with joined hands
Bend made as a courteous dance greeting
To change direction while completing a dance figure
Figure in which partners rotate together
One foot movement within a dance figure
Body part joined with another dancer’s during a figure
Musicians providing music for a social dance

answerNotes.CALLER: The caller names or announces figures. The dancers respond through the movements in the set.
answerNotes.PROMENADE: Promenade describes walking together in the dance. The word also names a public walkway in another setting.
answerNotes.DOSADO: Dosado is a common joined spelling of do-si-do. The clue describes the passing figure rather than asking for a pronunciation.
answerNotes.ALLEMANDE: Allemande is a traditional turning figure. Joined hands distinguish the action described here.

title: A Community Choir
description: Sing through familiar choral words for voices, shared notes, and the person guiding the group.
cardDescription: Sing through familiar choral words for voices, shared notes, and the person guiding the group.
focus: The clues name parts and performance ideas used in a choir. The musical meaning distinguishes several ordinary words.
solvingTip: Look for a voice part, a group, or a way singers combine their sounds.
words: Sound produced by a singer’s vocal organs
Lower standard treble choral voice part
Higher standard adult male choral voice part
Singing the same musical line together
Different notes combined to support a shared musical texture
Song whose melody is begun at different times by different groups
One section of words in a song
Open speech sound sustained in many sung syllables
Written music showing the parts of a composition
Person performing music with the voice
Person guiding the timing and expression of a choir

answerNotes.UNISON: Unison uses the same musical line. Harmony can combine different notes at the same time.
answerNotes.ROUND: A round repeats one melody with staggered starts. It names a musical structure rather than a circular shape.
answerNotes.SCORE: Score means written music here. It does not mean points earned in a game.
answerNotes.CONDUCTOR: A conductor guides the performing group. The clue does not refer to a railway worker.

title: An Evening Concert
description: Visit a live concert through familiar seating, admission, and performance words.
cardDescription: Visit a live concert through familiar seating, admission, and performance words.
focus: The clues move from arriving at the hall to listening and applauding. Some answers identify places, while others describe a printed guide or a musical feature.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a place, a printed guide, or an event during the performance.
words: Live performance of music for an audience
Admission record for a live music event
Entrance area outside a concert auditorium
Raised area occupied by concert performers
Fabric screen that may hang before a stage
Raised seating level above the main concert floor
Passage between rows in a concert hall
Person guiding concertgoers to their seats
Printed list of works or performers at a concert
Clapping that expresses an audience’s approval
Extra performance given after a concert’s planned ending
Assigned place for one member of the audience
Musical passage featuring one performer at a concert

answerNotes.PROGRAM: A concert program lists the works or performers. It is a guide to the event rather than the performance itself.
answerNotes.BALCONY: The balcony is an upper seating area. It differs from the ground-level rows nearer the stage.
answerNotes.ENCORE: An encore is additional music after the expected ending. The word is associated with requests for another performance.
answerNotes.SOLO: A solo features one musician. Accompanying players may still be heard beneath the featured part.

title: Humming a Familiar Tune
description: Follow a simple tune through words for sound, timing, and listening.
cardDescription: Follow a simple tune through words for sound, timing, and listening.
focus: The clues define everyday musical language. They do not require reading notation or recalling a particular song.
solvingTip: Look for a sound feature, a timing word, or an action done while enjoying music.
words: To sing with the lips closed
A recognizable melody that can be hummed
Sequence of notes heard as a musical line
One musical pitch or written sign for it
Written or performed silence within music
Recurring pulse kept while humming a tune
Speed at which a musical piece is performed
To perform a musical phrase again
Short connected group of musical notes
To pay attention to a musical sound

answerNotes.TEMPO: Tempo is the pace of the music. It differs from volume, which concerns loudness.
answerNotes.REST: A musical rest is a period of silence. It is part of the music rather than simply stopping a rehearsal.
answerNotes.PHRASE: A phrase is a short musical unit. It can be recognized as a connected idea within a longer melody.
answerNotes.HUM: Humming uses a closed mouth. The clue describes the action without asking for song words.
